cosy-lesson.title: Sitting Up Straight May Improve Your Mood (B1)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Posture ≠ slouching – the position in which someone holds their body when standing or sitting.

p.em: Example: Good posture improves lung capacity and alertness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Decision-making ≠ hesitation – the process of making choices, especially important ones.

p.em: Example: Sitting up straight boosts confidence in decision-making.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive ≠ physical – relating to the mental processes of perception and judgment.

p.em: Example: Proper alignment reduces cognitive fatigue during long study sessions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Upright ≠ slouched – vertical or erect in position.

p.em: Example: Maintaining an upright posture signals self-assurance.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mood ≠ apathy – a temporary state of mind or feeling.

p.em: Example: Slouching is linked to lower mood and fatigue.

cosy-blockquote.p: Alertness ≠ drowsiness – the state of being watchful and prompt to meet danger or emergency.

p.em: Example: Upright seating enhances mental alertness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Alignment ≠ distortion – arrangement in a straight line or in correct relative positions.

p.em: Example: Spinal alignment supports optimal blood flow to the brain.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ergonomic ≠ awkward – designed for efficiency and comfort in the working environment.

p.em: Example: Ergonomic chairs encourage healthy daily seating habits.

cosy-blockquote.p: Confidence ≠ self-doubt – the feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something.

p.em: Example: Adopting an upright posture instantly increases self-confidence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mechanism ≠ chaos – a system of parts working together in a machine or process.

p.em: Example: The physiological mechanism involves hormone regulation and oxygen intake.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does maintaining an upright posture influence respiratory efficiency and oxygen intake?
★ Are you conscious of your spinal alignment while working?

How does posture affect rapid executive decision-making under pressure?
★ Do you stand up during important phone calls or decisions?

What is the connection between physical stance and complex cognitive performance?
★ Have you noticed mental fog when slouching for hours?

Why is an upright sitting position associated with feelings of dominance and authority?
★ How does body language project confidence in business meetings?

How does physical body alignment modulate psychological mood state during stressful tasks?
★ Do physical stretches help relieve bad mood days?

What environmental factors increase mental alertness in an office space?
★ Does natural sunlight improve your work alertness?

Why is proper spinal alignment essential for preventing long-term muscular strain?
★ Have you ever used posture tracking apps or wearable devices?

What makes an office setup truly ergonomic for long computer sessions?
★ How have you customized your home desk setup?

How does confident body language reinforce inner emotional confidence?
★ Do you practice power posing before public speaking?

What neurobiological mechanism links spinal muscle contraction to emotion centers in the brain?
★ Are you intrigued by mind-body neurobiology research?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Adopting an upright posture triggers measurable hormonal changes that reduce stress. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Believe body language changes brain chemistry?

Complex decision-making is faster and more accurate when standing or sitting tall. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Prefer standing meetings over sitting discussions?

Physical posture plays a direct role in sustaining peak cognitive focus. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Notice your attention drop when slouching?

Remaining in an upright position during negotiations communicates authority effectively. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Conscious of your posture in meetings?

Improving daily posture is a more effective long-term strategy for mood regulation than medication. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Value physical alignment for emotional health?

Maintaining high mental alertness throughout the day requires hourly movement breaks. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Take movement breaks during work hours?

Correcting spinal alignment early prevents debilitating chronic musculoskeletal disorders. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ See a physical therapist for checkups?

Employers should provide fully adjustable ergonomic workstations for all desk employees. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should ergonomic furniture be mandatory in offices?

Projecting nonverbal confidence through body language improves professional success. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Judge people's confidence by their walk and posture?

Understanding the neurobiological mechanism of embodied cognition will transform mental healthcare. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Interested in embodied psychology research?

ul.li: Incorrect: Good posture may to improve mood. → Correct: Good posture may improve mood. ((Modal verb 'may' is followed by base verb without 'to'.))
Incorrect: I sit slouchedly at my desk. → Correct: I sit slouched at my desk. ((Use participle adjective 'slouched' to describe seating posture.))
